intro: Given at Sinai in fire and smoke, written by the finger of God on two tablets. The Catholic numbering follows Augustine: the first commandment includes the ban on images, and coveting is divided in two.

items.n: I am the Lord thy God: thou shalt not have strange gods before me.
Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain.
Remember that thou keep holy the sabbath day.
Honour thy father and thy mother.
Thou shalt not kill.
Thou shalt not commit adultery.
Thou shalt not steal.
Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.
Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's wife.
Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's goods.

intro: The opening of the Sermon on the Mount: eight blessings that turn the world's values upside down. Luke gives four, with four woes.

items.n: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Blessed are the meek: for they shall possess the land.
Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.
Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after justice: for they shall have their fill.
Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.
Blessed are the clean of heart: for they shall see God.
Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.
Blessed are they that suffer persecution for justice' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

intro: Seven times in John Jesus says 'I am' with an image — and several times without one, echoing the name God gave Moses at the bush: 'I AM WHO AM.'

items.n: I am the bread of life.
I am the light of the world.
I am the door of the sheep.
I am the good shepherd.
I am the resurrection and the life.
I am the way, and the truth, and the life.
I am the true vine.
Before Abraham was made, I am.
items.k: John 8:58 — and they took up stones

intro: The seven sentences spoken from the cross, gathered from all four Gospels, in the traditional order.

items.n: Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.
Amen I say to thee, this day thou shalt be with me in paradise.
Woman, behold thy son. Behold thy mother.
My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
items.k: Matthew 27:46; Mark 15:34 — the first line of Psalm 21 (22)

items.n: I thirst.
It is consummated.
Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit.

sub: the numbered lists of the catechism, from Scripture
intro: The lists every Catholic child once learned by heart, each with the verse it comes from.

items.n: The seven gifts of the Holy Spirit: wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, piety, fear of the Lord.
The fruits of the Holy Spirit: charity, joy, peace, patience, benignity, goodness, longanimity, mildness, faith, modesty, continency, chastity.
The three theological virtues: faith, hope and charity — 'and the greatest of these is charity'.
The four cardinal virtues: prudence, justice, fortitude, temperance.
The corporal works of mercy: feed the hungry, give drink to the thirsty, clothe the naked, shelter the stranger, visit the sick, visit the imprisoned, bury the dead.
The two greatest commandments: love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart; love thy neighbour as thyself.
The Golden Rule: all things whatsoever you would that men should do to you, do you also to them.

intro: Four lists, always in three groups of four, Peter always first and Judas always last. With each: how tradition says he died.

items.n: Simon Peter
items.k: fisherman of Bethsaida; the rock; crucified head-down in Rome under Nero, c. 64

items.n: Andrew
items.k: Peter's brother, the first called; crucified on an X-shaped cross at Patras

items.n: James the Greater
items.k: son of Zebedee; beheaded by Herod Agrippa in Jerusalem, 44 — the first apostle to die (Acts 12)

items.n: John
items.k: his brother, 'the disciple whom Jesus loved'; the only one to die in old age, at Ephesus

items.n: Philip
items.k: of Bethsaida; 'come and see'; died at Hierapolis in Phrygia

items.n: Bartholomew (Nathanael)
items.k: 'an Israelite in whom there is no guile'; flayed in Armenia

items.n: Thomas
items.k: the twin, who doubted and then said 'my Lord and my God'; speared in India

items.n: Matthew (Levi)
items.k: the tax collector, the evangelist; martyred in Ethiopia by tradition

items.n: James the Less
items.k: son of Alphaeus; thrown from the Temple and clubbed, 62

items.n: Jude (Thaddaeus)
items.k: 'not Iscariot'; martyred in Persia with Simon

items.n: Simon the Zealot
items.k: the Cananean; sawn in two, by one tradition

items.n: Judas Iscariot
items.k: the treasurer; the betrayer; hanged himself. Matthias was chosen by lot in his place (Acts 1).
